title: CLR/10/2017 of Satpal Vs Mohd. Aarif

paras.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
CIVIL REVISION NO. 10 OF 2017
Satpal ÖÖÖDefendant/Revisionist
 Versus
Mohd. Aarif ÖÖ..Plaintiff/Respondent
Present : Mr. Arvind Vashistha, Senior Advocate assisted by Mr.
Bharat Singh Mehra, Advocate for the defendant/revisionist.
 Mr. Piyush Garg, Advocate for the plaintiff/respondent.
Honíble Sudhanshu Dhulia, J.
 This is a defendantís revision under Section
25 of the Provincial Small Causes Court Act. A suit for
rent and eviction was filed by the plaintiff/respondent
before the Judge, Small Causes Court, Dehradun for
payment of rent and eviction against his tenant i.e. the
revisionist, defendant before the court below, which has
been decreed by the court below vide its order dated
28.11.2016.
2. There is a specific finding of the Trial Court
that the provisions of Uttar Pradesh Urban Buildings
(Regulation of Letting, Rent and Eviction) Act, 1972 are not
applicable in the matter as the premises in question which
is a shop was constructed in the year 1990 and the tenant
has defaulted in payment of rent, etc.
3. The defendant/revisionist is being
represented by Mr. Arvind Vashistha, Senior Advocate
assisted by Mr. Bharat Singh Mehra, Advocate and the
plaintiff/respondent is being represented by Mr. Piyush
Garg, Advocate.

2
4. Learned Senior Counsel for the revisionist
very fairly submits before this Court that subject to the
consent of the plaintiff/respondent, he would not press his
revision if a reasonable time is granted to the revisionist to
vacate the premises in question. The premises in question
is a shop at 16/5, Dhamawala Mohalla, Dehradun.
5. Learned counsel for the landlord/respondent
states that the landlord/respondent is willing to give two
years time, from today to the tenant/revisionist to vacate
the premises. This period is acceptable to the
tenant/revisionist.
6. In view thereof, subject to the consent of both
the parties who are being represented by their respective
counsels, no interference is liable to be made with the
order dated 28.11.2016 passed by the Judge, Small
Causes Court subject, however, to the following conditions
which shall be binding upon both the parties. These
conditions are as follows:
 (I) The revisionist shall remain in the
premises in question for the period of two years
i.e. till 09.02.2019 subject to an undertaking
given by him before the Trial Court within a
period of three weeks from the date of procuring
a certified copy of this order. He shall give an
undertaking that he shall vacate the premises in
question on or before 09.02.2019 and handover
the vacant and peaceful possession of the
premises in question to the
respondent/landlord.
 (II) That the revisionist shall also
undertake to deposit the entire decreetal
amount before the Trial Court within a period of

3
two months from the date of procurement of
certified copy of this order, which shall be
subject to the adjustment of amount already
deposited before the court below, if any.
 (III) The revisionist shall continue to
pay the rent for the use and occupation of the
premises in question on the 7th day of each
succeeding month till vacation of the
accommodation.
 (IV) The revisionist shall not induct
any other person in the premises in question.
 (V) It is further made clear that in the
event of default of any of the aforesaid
conditions, the revisionist shall not be entitled
to continue in the premises in question upto
09.02.2019 as indicated above and the decree
shall be executed forthwith.
7. With the directions as aforesaid, civil revision
finally stands disposed.
8. Stay application (CLMA No.1046 of 2017) and
Urgency application (IA No. 865 of 2017) also stand
disposed accordingly.
